questions.prompt: With your U01 code closed: what do remainingTitles and totalMinutes take in, what do they return, and what must they leave untouched?

keyPoints.text: remainingTitles keeps only tasks whose done flag is exactly false, and keeps them in their original order
keyPoints.quote: return titles whose done is exactly false, in original order

keyPoints.text: Each task is an object with a string title and a boolean done
totalMinutes adds up nonnegative integer minutes
Neither function may change the caller's array
Empty input is a defined case: [] for the titles, 0 for the minutes
const on the result array does not stop you from mutating it, so mutation safety is about what you write, not the keyword
keyPoints.quote: const prevents rebinding; it does not freeze an array

questions.prompt: A function logs 7 and its caller adds the function's return value to 1. What does the caller see, and why?

keyPoints.text: Logging only shows the value; it is not the function's result
keyPoints.quote: Logging displays a value but does not return it

keyPoints.text: Only return hands a value back to the caller
keyPoints.quote: Parameters receive inputs and return sends a result to the caller

keyPoints.text: With no return statement the call evaluates to undefined, and undefined + 1 is NaN, which is what you observe
undefined is an ordinary JavaScript value you can reason about
keyPoints.quote: Values include numbers, strings, booleans and undefined

keyPoints.text: A function is a named, reusable transformation from inputs to an output, so its output is what it returns
keyPoints.quote: a function names a reusable transformation

questions.prompt: Trace countWarm([19, 20, 24]) and countWarm([]) out loud. Where is the boundary, and how would you prove a changed boundary with a test?

keyPoints.text: 19 is below the threshold, so the count does not move
20 and 24 both count, so the result is 2
keyPoints.quote: For 20 it becomes 1, and 24 makes it 2

keyPoints.text: The comparison operator decides whether the threshold itself counts
keyPoints.quote: The boundary is inclusive because of >=

keyPoints.text: An empty array never enters the loop, so the initial 0 is returned
keyPoints.quote: Empty input never enters the loop, so returns 0

keyPoints.text: Trace concrete values by hand before trusting the syntax
keyPoints.quote: Trace a concrete example on paper before adding syntax

keyPoints.text: A test pins the boundary by comparing actual behaviour to a stated expectation
keyPoints.quote: A test assertion compares actual behavior to a stated expectation
